question: An analyst begins every chat in her weekly reporting project by typing the same six lines about house style, the sections required and how figures should be rounded. What is the most effective first change?
options: A) Ask Claude at the start of each chat to recall the style used in her previous conversations.
B) Keep the six lines in a note and paste them at the start of each chat so nothing gets forgotten.
C) Upload a document holding the six lines and point Claude at it whenever she opens a new chat.
D) Move those standing lines into the project's instructions so every chat there starts with them.
correct_answers: D) Move those standing lines into the project's instructions so every chat there starts with them.
explanations: Asking Claude to recall earlier style is unreliable and does not make the requirement durable.
A note reduces typing but still relies on her pasting it correctly every single time.
Uploaded documents are background knowledge; a standing rule about how to work belongs in the instructions.
Correct. A requirement repeated in every chat of the same project belongs in the project instructions, where it applies automatically and stops depending on her remembering it.
